title: Strict coherent tensor tower comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. Write $L^0_W=\lim\circ U_W$ and $r_W=\operatorname{leftAdjoint}(L^0_W)$ for ordinary coherent reduction, equipped with its specified adjunction $r_W\dashv L^0_W$ and unit $\eta^0_W$; concretely its components are quotient extension $B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}M$ and its transitions are induced by the actual quotient maps. A superscript $c$ means termwise application to cochain complexes. For a coherent complex $C$, let $\lambda_C:q_W((L^0_W)^c C)\to\mathcal L_W(q^s_WC)$ be the canonical right-derived limit unit, with the exact-restriction/localization factorization inserted (the map named pullbackTensorLimitUnit). Let $a_{W,n}:B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}(-)\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{W,n}r_W$ be the finite evaluation of ordinary reduction fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism whose transpose under the quotient-extension/restriction adjunction is, for every $A_W$-module $M$, exactly $\pi_n\circ\eta^0_{W,M}:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}e_{W,n}r_WM$, where $\pi_n$ is the actual $n$th limit projection of $U_Wr_WM$ followed by its recorded evaluation/scalar-restriction identification; it is also applied termwise to complexes. For arbitrary complexes $P,Q$ of $A_W$-modules, let $\operatorname{Tot}_s$ be the ordinary direct-sum total tensor on $\mathscr S_W$ with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes dy$. Let $T(P,Q)=J_W(U_W^c\operatorname{Tot}_s(r_W^cP,r_W^cQ))$ and let $B_\otimes^0(P,Q)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}\operatorname{Tot}_{B_{W,n}}(B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}P,B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}Q)$ with actual quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. At level $n$ define $d_{P,Q,n}$ by reordering, the prescribed evaluation/total-tensor isomorphism of the coherent calculus, and the tensor of the two inverse reduction-evaluation maps $a_{W,n,P}^{-1},a_{W,n,Q}^{-1}$, all under $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$. There exists a unique strict tower isomorphism $d_{P,Q}:T(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_\otimes^0(P,Q)$ with exactly these components for every $n$. This is pullbackTensorTensorTower_existsUnique for arbitrary unbounded $P,Q$, without K-flatness or termwise-flatness hypotheses.

proof.text:
Suppress $W$, and write $	au_n:B_{n+1}	o B_n$ and $t_n$ for actual horizontal transitions. For an $A$-module $M$ put $
u_n=\pi_n\eta^0_M$. The limit-cone identity gives $t_n
u_{n+1}=
u_n$. The stipulated scalar-adjunction transpose of $a_{n,M}$ says precisely $a_{n,M}(b\otimes x)=b
u_n(x)$ on local pure tensors. Consequently
$$t_n a_{n+1,M}(b\otimes x)=	au_n(b)
u_n(x)=a_{n,M}(	au_n(b)\otimes x).$$
Pure tensors generate the presheaf tensor, and the sheafification universal property extends this equality to the sheaf tensor. Thus $a_n$ intertwines the actual quotient transition with that of $rM$, and its inverse does too, by composing the square with $a_{n+1}^{-1}$ and $a_n^{-1}$. Apply this to every $P^k$ and $Q^k$; naturality of $a_n$ for the differentials makes these comparisons cochain isomorphisms with the same transition squares.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; the scalar-unit and cone calculation uses exactly the adjunction normalization in the item.

proof.text:
Put $C=r^cP$ and $D=r^cQ$. Evaluation $e_n$ is the inverse image of the vertical inclusion with its identity coefficient identification. Apply lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence to this ringed-topos morphism to obtain a cochain isomorphism
$$\kappa_n:e_n\operatorname{Tot}_s(C,D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{B_n}(e_nC,e_nD).$$
This is the prescribed evaluation/total-tensor isomorphism: lem-coef-semilinear-tensor-evaluation fixes the ordinary evaluation comparison and its chain summands for the chosen models. On every $(p,q)$ summand both comparisons are that ordinary evaluation comparison; the direct-sum universal property makes the chain maps equal. In particular the inverse-model-chain convention and the displayed forward $\kappa_n$ agree. The cochain theorem applies to arbitrary unbounded complexes, with the same $(-1)^p$ differential and no flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, ordinary total-complex comparison in its proof; representative normalization supplied by the cited semilinear evaluation node.

proof.text:
Apply lem-pur-system-cochain-tensor-reduction to $C,D$ and $n\le n+1$. Its identity identifies the horizontal scalar-extension adjoint of the total-system transition with the scalar tensor comparison followed by the tensor of the two horizontal adjoints, under the prescribed evaluation comparisons. Transpose through the scalar-extension/restriction adjunction. Equivalently, on every evaluated tensor summand the resulting transition is
$$x\otimes y\longmapsto t_n^C(x)\otimes t_n^D(y).$$
Thus $\kappa_n$ intertwines the actual total-system transition with this tensor transition, before localization. This uses the cochain identity of the cited node, not a claim that maps of derived evaluations lift. Restrict scalars along $A\to B_n$: the underlying section maps are unchanged, and $A\to B_n$ is $A\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$, so the same square is an equality of $A$-linear cochain maps.

source.place: Tag 07A4 ordinary total-complex construction and the ringed sequence site preceding Tag 0941; the horizontal tensor-adjoint identity is the statement of the cited cochain-reduction node.

proof.text:
After the specified reordering $J$, define $d_n$ to be $\operatorname{Res}_n$ of $\kappa_n$ followed by $\operatorname{Tot}_{B_n}(a_{n,P}^{-1},a_{n,Q}^{-1})$. This is exactly the component prescribed in the item. Tensor the two transition squares from step 1 and paste them with step 3. The result is
$$d_n\,t_n^T=t_n^{B_\otimes^0}\,d_{n+1}.$$
The target transition is the actual quotient transition: on a $(p,q)$ summand it sends $(b\otimes x)\otimes(c\otimes y)$ to $(\tau_n(b)\otimes x)\otimes(\tau_n(c)\otimes y)$. Functoriality of total tensor gives the pasted equality on complexes. The reordering just evaluates the same section maps in the opposite order. Identities and composites of adjacent transitions give the equality for every arrow of $\mathbf N^{op}$.

source.place: Tag 0941, ringed sequence-site construction preceding lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; elementary pasting of steps 1 and 3 with the specified tower definitions.

proof.text: The maps $d_n$ therefore form a strict tower morphism. Each is an isomorphism, since its factors are cochain isomorphisms and scalar restriction is a functor. From $d_nt_n^T=t_n^{B_\otimes^0}d_{n+1}$, compose with the two component inverses to obtain the transition square for $(d_n^{-1})_n$. These inverses form an inverse tower morphism, since both composites are identities at every level. Finally any tower isomorphism with the stipulated components has the same forward natural transformation, hence the same inverse. This proves existence and uniqueness for the arbitrary $P,Q$ fixed above.

theorem pullbackTensorTensorTower_existsUnique (W : Scheme.{u})
    (P Q : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E W) ℤ) :
    ∃! e : pullbackTensorRestrictedTower l E W
      ((coefficientTotalTensor.{u, u + 1, u}
        (coefficientSequenceTopology (ProEt.topology W))
        (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E W)).obj
        ((((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P),
          (((pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q))) ≅
      (integralOperationsTensorTowerFunctor l E W).obj (P,Q),
      ∀ n : ℕ, e.app (op n) = pullbackTensorTensorTowerLevel l E W P Q n
